The helpers iterate_with_offset(param_name, start, offset, resp_pages, resp_complete), iterate_with_cursor() and iterate_with_link_url() build next_req for the usual designs. resps_data(resps, resp_data) combines the parsed bodies, and resps_successes(), resps_failures(), resps_requests() and resps_ok() (httr2 1.2.2) sort the list. When the number of pages is known, req_perform_parallel(reqs, max_active = 10, on_error = c("stop", "return", "continue")) sends the requests at once, and req_perform_sequential() one by one with the same interface. The local server reports the total in the X-Total-Count header.

library(httr2)
source("scenario.R")

# A local test server: /books returns one page, "limit" rows from "offset",
# and reports the total in the X-Total-Count header.
shelf_api <- function(books, port) {
  plumber::pr() |>
    plumber::pr_set_serializer(plumber::serializer_unboxed_json()) |>
    plumber::pr_get("/books", \(res, limit = "5", offset = "0") {
      rows <- as.integer(offset) + seq_len(as.integer(limit))
      res$setHeader("X-Total-Count", nrow(books))
      books[rows[rows <= nrow(books)], c("title", "isbn", "year")]
    }) |>
    plumber::pr_run(host = "127.0.0.1", port = port, docs = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
}

srv <- callr::r_bg(shelf_api, args = list(books = books, port = 8765L))
base <- "http://127.0.0.1:8765"
req <- request(base) |>
  req_url_path_append("books") |>
  req_url_query(limit = 5) |>
  req_retry(max_tries = 20, retry_on_failure = TRUE, backoff = \(i) 0.25)
invisible(req_perform(req))

# How many pages? The total is in a header.
total <- \(resp) as.integer(resp_header(resp, "X-Total-Count"))
pages <- \(resp) ceiling(total(resp) / 5)

# req_perform_iterative(): each request is made from the previous response.
resps <- req_perform_iterative(
  req,
  next_req = iterate_with_offset("offset", start = 0, offset = 5,
                                 resp_pages = pages),
  progress = FALSE
)
length(resps)
#> [1] 4
vapply(resps, resp_status, integer(1L))
#> [1] 200 200 200 200
req_get_url(resp_request(resps[[2L]]))
#> [1] "http://127.0.0.1:8765/books?limit=5&offset=5"

# resps_data() combines the parsed bodies; here, a data frame per page.
page_data <- \(resp) resp_body_json(resp, simplifyVector = TRUE)
shelf <- resps_data(resps, page_data)
dim(shelf)
#> [1] 16  3
shelf$title[c(1L, 16L)]
#> [1] "The Dispossessed" "Salt and Static"

# max_reqs caps the loop (the default is 20).
two <- req_perform_iterative(
  req,
  next_req = iterate_with_offset("offset", start = 0, offset = 5,
                                 resp_pages = pages),
  max_reqs = 2,
  progress = FALSE
)
length(two)
#> [1] 2

# When the page count is known, build the requests and send them together.
offsets <- seq(0L, 15L, by = 5L)
reqs <- lapply(offsets, \(o) req |> req_url_query(offset = o))
par_resps <- req_perform_parallel(reqs, progress = FALSE)
vapply(par_resps, resp_status, integer(1L))
#> [1] 200 200 200 200
identical(resps_data(par_resps, page_data), shelf)
#> [1] TRUE

# req_perform_sequential() has the same interface, one request at a time.
seq_resps <- req_perform_sequential(reqs, progress = FALSE)
identical(resps_data(seq_resps, page_data), shelf)
#> [1] TRUE

# on_error = "continue" keeps going and returns the failures with the rest.
bad <- c(reqs[1:2], list(request(base) |> req_url_path_append("nope")))
mixed <- req_perform_parallel(bad, on_error = "continue", progress = FALSE)
vapply(mixed, \(x) class(x)[1L], character(1L))
#> [1] "httr2_response" "httr2_response" "httr2_http_404"
length(resps_successes(mixed))
#> [1] 2
length(resps_failures(mixed))
#> [1] 1
resps_ok(mixed)
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE

invisible(srv$kill())

Source: httr2 package documentation: req_perform_iterative, iterate_with_offset, req_perform_parallel and resps_successes

The sixteen books come in four pages of five, and resp_pages computed the number of pages from the total in the header. resps_data() rebuilt the full data frame, identical for the iterative, parallel and sequential versions. max_reqs caps the loop. With on_error = "continue" the failing request becomes an error object in the list (here class httr2_http_404) and the others still complete; resps_ok() is a logical vector of the successes. Since httr2 1.1.1, req_perform_parallel() lifts many restrictions (it checks the cache before and after each request and can refresh OAuth tokens) and its pool argument was replaced by max_active; the argument was removed in httr2 1.2.0. req_perform_iterative() is no longer experimental since httr2 1.0.4.

Caching

req_cache(req, path, use_on_error = FALSE, debug, max_age, max_n, max_size) stores the responses to GET requests that have status 200 and at least one standard caching header (Expires, ETag, Last-Modified, Cache-Control), unless Cache-Control: no-store forbids it. Most API requests are not cacheable; static files often are. A request is still sent to check that the cached value is up to date, unless the cached value is still fresh by max-age, in which case the server is not contacted at all. path is a directory that is created automatically (tempfile() for a session cache, tools::R_user_dir() for a persistent one); the cache prunes itself to max_age, max_n and max_size (the default size limit is 1 GB). debug = TRUE (or options(httr2_cache_debug = TRUE)) prints messages about cache hits and misses; they include a hash that is not printed in the example. httr2 1.3.0 requires rlang 1.3.0, which changes the hash that names the cache files, so files cached by an earlier version are silently ignored and cleaned up over time.

library(httr2)

# A local test server: /count increments a counter on every request that
# reaches it, and /fresh/count marks the response cacheable for 60 seconds.
shelf_api <- function(port) {
  seen <- new.env()
  seen$plain <- 0L
  seen$fresh <- 0L
  plumber::pr() |>
    plumber::pr_set_serializer(plumber::serializer_unboxed_json()) |>
    plumber::pr_get("/count", \() {
      seen$plain <- seen$plain + 1L
      list(served = seen$plain)
    }) |>
    plumber::pr_get("/fresh/count", \(res) {
      seen$fresh <- seen$fresh + 1L
      res$setHeader("Cache-Control", "max-age=60")
      list(served = seen$fresh)
    }) |>
    plumber::pr_run(host = "127.0.0.1", port = port, docs = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
}

srv <- callr::r_bg(shelf_api, args = list(port = 8765L))
base <- "http://127.0.0.1:8765"
request(base) |>
  req_url_path_append("count") |>
  req_retry(max_tries = 20, retry_on_failure = TRUE, backoff = \(i) 0.25) |>
  req_perform() |>
  invisible()

served <- \(req) resp_body_json(req_perform(req))$served

# No cache headers: every call reaches the server (the first count was above).
plain <- request(base) |> req_url_path_append("count")
served(plain)
#> [1] 2
served(plain)
#> [1] 3

# A cacheable response with req_cache(): the second call does not.
cache_dir <- tempfile("shelf-cache")
fresh <- request(base) |>
  req_url_path_append("fresh", "count") |>
  req_cache(cache_dir)
served(fresh)
#> [1] 1
served(fresh)
#> [1] 1
length(list.files(cache_dir))
#> [1] 1

# The same request without req_cache() goes to the server again.
served(request(base) |> req_url_path_append("fresh", "count"))
#> [1] 2

# Only GET responses with status 200 and a caching header are stored: the
# plain route above has none, so a cache would store nothing for it.
cache_dir_2 <- tempfile("shelf-cache")
cached_plain <- plain |> req_cache(cache_dir_2)
invisible(served(cached_plain))
length(list.files(cache_dir_2))
#> [1] 0

invisible(srv$kill())

Source: httr2 package documentation: req_cache

The route that sets Cache-Control: max-age=60 is served once: the second call with req_cache() returned served 1 again without reaching the server, and left one file in the cache directory; the same request without req_cache() reached the server (count 2). A response without a caching header, like /count, is not stored (zero files). Since httr2 1.2.3 a custom req_error() is respected on cache hits.

Testing without a server: mocking

The best test of code that calls an API does not call it. with_mocked_responses(mock, code) and local_mocked_responses(mock) replace the network call of req_perform() (and of req_perform_parallel(), req_perform_sequential() and req_perform_iterative() since httr2 1.2.0) for the duration of code or of the calling function. mock is a function from the request to a response, or a list of responses served in order. response() and response_json() build responses of any status. They were introduced in httr2 1.0.0 as the replacement for with_mock() and local_mock(), which were deprecated then and removed in 1.2.0. Responses retrieved from a mock include the originating request, as real ones do (httr2 1.2.3). local_mocked_responses() is the form used in test_that() blocks of a package (Testing with testthat); this needs no server, no port and no network.

library(httr2)

# A function that talks to a web API (a placeholder host; never contacted).
book_title <- function(isbn) {
  request("https://api.example.com/v1") |>
    req_url_path_append("books", isbn) |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_json() |>
    _$title
}

# with_mocked_responses(): the mock replaces req_perform()'s network call.
# A function receives the request and returns a response.
with_mocked_responses(
  \(req) response_json(body = list(title = "Ten Winters")),
  book_title("9780013001331")
)
#> [1] "Ten Winters"

# The function sees the request, so one mock can serve several URLs.
router <- \(req) {
  if (grepl("/books/9780013001331$", req$url)) {
    response_json(body = list(title = "Ten Winters"))
  } else {
    response_json(status_code = 404L, body = list(error = "no such book"))
  }
}
with_mocked_responses(router, book_title("9780013001331"))
#> [1] "Ten Winters"
with_mocked_responses(
  router,
  tryCatch(book_title("0"), httr2_http_404 = \(e) conditionMessage(e))
)
#> [1] "HTTP 404 Not Found."

# A list is served in order, one response per request.
with_mocked_responses(
  list(
    response_json(body = list(title = "Ten Winters")),
    response_json(body = list(title = "Salt and Static"))
  ),
  c(book_title("1"), book_title("2"))
)
#> [1] "Ten Winters"     "Salt and Static"

# local_mocked_responses() lasts until the function that calls it returns:
# the form to use inside test_that() blocks.
offline_title <- function() {
  local_mocked_responses(\(req) response_json(body = list(title = "Offline")))
  book_title("anything")
}
offline_title()
#> [1] "Offline"

# response() builds any response, including a non-JSON one.
text_resp <- response(
  status_code = 200L,
  headers = list("Content-Type" = "text/plain"),
  body = charToRaw("hello")
)
hello <- \() {
  request("https://api.example.com/hello") |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_string()
}
with_mocked_responses(\(req) text_resp, hello())
#> [1] "hello"

Source: httr2 package documentation: with_mocked_responses and response

The function under test, book_title(), is the kind of wrapper a package contains. The mock sees the request, so router() served one URL and answered 404 to the others, which triggered the real error path of the code under test, httr2_http_404. One limit, seen with the checked version of httr2: a mocked 429 response is not retried by req_retry() (the call raised HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. at once), so retry logic is tested against the local server, as in the previous section, or by testing the is_transient and after functions on their own with response() objects.

OAuth, streaming and background requests

The remaining parts of httr2 need a real server or a user, so this section is prose. The req_oauth_*() functions implement the OAuth flows: req_oauth_auth_code() (opens a browser; for interactive use), req_oauth_client_credentials() and req_oauth_bearer_jwt() (server-to-server), req_oauth_device(), req_oauth_password(), req_oauth_refresh() and req_oauth_token_exchange(). They take an oauth_client() and cache the token, encrypted, in a directory (oauth_cache_path(), which defaults to a standard R user cache directory since httr2 1.3.0); tokens are refreshed automatically and oauth_cache_prune() and oauth_cache_clear() delete old ones. httr2 1.3.0 raised the default margin before expiry at which a cached token is treated as expired from 5 to 30 seconds (the expiry_margin argument) and fixed the pruning of cached tokens, which had not matched the encrypted files written to disk. The httr2 OAuth article is httr2 package documentation: OAuth. Credentials never belong in the script; use Sys.getenv() and obfuscate().

Large or open-ended responses are streamed rather than loaded: req_perform_connection() returns a response whose body is a connection, read in pieces with resp_stream_lines(), resp_stream_sse() (server-sent events) and resp_stream_bytes() (httr2 1.0.4; req_perform_stream() is superseded by it, and soft-deprecated since httr2 1.2.0). req_perform_promise() (httr2 1.0.3) returns a promise so a request can run in the background of a Shiny app or an async pipeline; the Parallel and Asynchronous Computing page puts it in context. is_online() wraps curl::has_internet(). httr2_translate() (httr2 1.2.3) and curl_translate() turn a request into the equivalent curl command and back, which is useful for copying a call from an API’s documentation.

JSON with jsonlite

JSON is the body format of most web APIs, and httr2 reads and writes it with jsonlite: req_body_json(req, data, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 22, null = "null") calls jsonlite::toJSON(), and resp_body_json(resp, simplifyVector = FALSE, ...) calls jsonlite::fromJSON(). The defaults differ in one important way: httr2 writes length-one vectors as JSON scalars (auto_unbox = TRUE), whereas toJSON() on its own writes them as one-element arrays, and resp_body_json() returns lists (simplifyVector = FALSE), while jsonlite::fromJSON() simplifies by default. simplifyVector = TRUE turns an array of records into a data frame, the form that data.frame code wants (the scripts above do it for the /books route); digits = 22 keeps the full double precision of numbers on the way out. The rules of simplification and the handling of NA and NULL belong to Serialization: RDS, RData and JSON. For XML and HTML bodies, resp_body_xml() and resp_body_html() use xml2.

Pitfalls

  • A download that "worked". download.file() returns 0 or a non-zero status, and with several URLs it may not raise an error at all. Test the value, and for a vector of URLs read attr(status, "retvals"). Never assume the file is there because the call returned.

  • A text-mode transfer on Windows. mode = "w" (the default) changes line endings and corrupts binary files; the damage is invisible on Linux and macOS. Always pass mode = "wb" for anything that is not text.

  • Secrets in code and in logs. A token or password belongs in an environment variable (Sys.getenv("SHELF_API_TOKEN")), a .Renviron file outside version control or a secrets store; never in a URL (https://user:password@host/ shows up in server logs) and never in a script that is committed. Printing a request is safe for Authorization and for headers marked .redact; printing req_get_headers(req, redacted = "reveal"), a saved log or curlGetHeaders() output of an authenticated URL is not.

  • Unescaped path segments and query values. URLencode() leaves reserved characters alone, so it is wrong for a query value (reserved = TRUE, or req_url_query(), which encodes for you); req_url_path_append() does not escape, so curl::curl_escape() a segment that came from data.

  • Treating a 404 as a connection error, or the reverse. HTTP errors are httr2_http_<status>; failures to connect, resolve or finish in time are httr2_failure. Handle them by class, and use req_error(body = ) so the R error carries what the API said.

  • Retrying what must not be repeated. req_retry() is safe for GET; for a POST that creates a record, check that the API is idempotent or uses an idempotency key. Without max_tries (or max_seconds) httr2 makes only two attempts.

  • Polling with Sys.sleep(). Use req_retry() with retry_on_failure = TRUE, or a loop with a limit, as the examples do; an unbounded while loop that waits for a service hangs forever when the service never comes up.

  • The default 60 seconds. options(timeout) limits the time without a response, not the whole transfer, and 60 seconds is too short for large files; set it in the script with max() so a user’s higher value stays.

  • Tests that depend on the internet. A test that calls a real API fails when the network, the API or the credentials change. Mock the responses (with_mocked_responses(), local_mocked_responses()) or serve them locally, and guard live tests with testthat::skip_if_offline() or an environment variable.

  • Reading a CSV from https:// on an old R. Before R 3.3.0 read.csv("https://...") needed a method choice on Windows; since 4.2.0 nothing needs to be done (R FAQ 7.43).

Version notes

The R rows are from R NEWS (R NEWS for R 3.x and R NEWS for R 4.x); the httr2 rows are from the package’s own NEWS (httr2 package documentation: Changelog). Only the entries relevant to this page are listed.

Version Change

R 3.2.0

libcurl is available as an optional method: capabilities("libcurl"), libcurlVersion(), curlGetHeaders(), download.file(method = "libcurl") (several URLs at once, redirections) and url(method = "libcurl"), with the option url.method

R 3.2.2

on non-Windows platforms download.file(method = "auto") chooses libcurl for https:// and ftps:// URLs when it is available

R 3.4.0

on Unix-alikes the default methods of download.file() and url() choose "libcurl" except for file:// URLs; the "wget" and "curl" methods give an R error rather than a non-zero return value when the external command fails

R 3.6.0

download.file() and url() get the argument headers for custom HTTP headers (for example basic authentication)

R 4.0.3

the option timeout can be set from R_DEFAULT_INTERNET_TIMEOUT; libcurl-based access, including curlGetHeaders(), now respects timeout

R 4.1.0

curlGetHeaders() gets the arguments timeout and TLS

R 4.1.1

ftp:// URLs are deprecated; the non-default "internal" method is deprecated for http:// and ftp://

R 4.2.0

on Windows download.file(method = "auto") and url(method = "default") use libcurl for everything except file://; the "internal" method supports only file://; "wininet" no longer supports ftp://; libcurl is required to build R from source

R 4.2.2

on Windows, R_LIBCURL_SSL_REVOKE_BEST_EFFORT switches to best-effort certificate revocation checks for the libcurl method

R 4.3.0

download.file() gives a helpful error for an invalid download.file.method option; libcurl 8.x is accepted by configure

R 4.5.0

install.packages() and download.packages() download packages simultaneously with libcurl; download.file() reports the outcome of individual files

R 4.5.2

install.packages() and download.packages() again consult download.file.method when the method is unspecified

R 4.6.0

credentials for basic authentication with the libcurl method can be provided in a netrc file named by options("netrc")

httr2 1.0.0 (2023-11-14)

req_perform_iterative(), req_perform_parallel() and req_perform_sequential(); resps_successes() and friends; all errors inherit from httr2_error (httr2_failure, httr2_http_<status>); local_mocked_responses() and with_mocked_responses() replace local_mock() and with_mock(); req_url_query(.multi = ); resp_has_body(), resp_check_content_type(); cache pruning arguments in req_cache(); resp_body_json() caches the parsed value

httr2 1.1.0 (2025-01-18)

req_retry() circuit breaking and max_tries = 2 by default; req_headers_redacted(); resp_request(); req_url_query(.space = ); url_modify() and url_parse() with curl::curl_parse_url(); req_perform_connection() no longer experimental; is_online()

httr2 1.1.1 (2025-03-08)

req_throttle() uses a token bucket; req_headers() redacts Authorization; req_dry_run() pretty-prints JSON and omits volatile headers; req_perform_parallel() supports retry, throttle, OAuth and the cache; HTTR2_VERBOSITY

httr2 1.2.0 (2025-07-13)

with_mock() and local_mock() removed; req_perform_stream() soft-deprecated for req_perform_connection(); redacted headers are no longer serialised to disk; URL construction uses curl::curl_modify_url(); req_get_url() and the other req_get_*() introspection functions; last_request_json() and last_response_json(); resp_timing(); mocks for the parallel, sequential and iterative performers

httr2 1.2.3 (2026-06-23)

req_throttle() can enforce several limits at once; httr2_translate(); mocked and cached responses carry the request; req_error() is applied on cache hits

httr2 1.3.0 (2026-07-13)

OAuth cache pruning fixed; oauth_cache_path() defaults to an R user cache directory; oauth_cache_prune(); expiry_margin (30 s by default); requires rlang 1.3.0, which changes the hash that names cached files

Source: httr2 package documentation: Changelog

The NEWS of R-devel (the upcoming 4.7.0, not released) lists no change to download.file(), url(), curlGetHeaders() or URLencode().

Where older tutorials differ

Much of the advice on the web about R and HTTP predates httr2 1.0.0 (2023) and the Windows libcurl default (R 4.2.0). It still works in many cases, and it is not wrong to read it; it is a map of what replaced what.

Older tutorial Today Why Stable in

RCurl::getURL(), getForm(), postForm()

httr2 (or curl)

RCurl is a separate binding to libcurl; httr and httr2 are built on the curl package, and httr2 is the one the httr authors recommend

httr2 1.0.0

httr::GET(url), httr::content(r, "parsed"), httr::stop_for_status(r)

request(url) |> req_perform() |> resp_body_json()

httr is superseded and only maintained to stay on CRAN; httr2 raises the HTTP error for you

httr2 1.0.0

httr::add_headers(), authenticate(), config(ssl_verifypeer = 0), set_config()

req_headers(), req_auth_basic(), req_options() on one request

no global configuration: every setting is on the request value, and Authorization is redacted when printed

httr2 1.0.0, 1.1.1

httr::POST(url, body = list(...), encode = "json")

req_body_json() or req_body_form()

the body type is a function, not an argument

httr2 1.0.0

paste0(url, "?genre=", genre, "&limit=", n)

req_url_query(genre = genre, limit = n)

escaping and vectors are handled

httr2 1.0.0

a hand-written for loop around try(GET(url)) with Sys.sleep()

req_retry() and req_throttle()

honours Retry-After, backs off with jitter, one token bucket per host

httr2 1.0.0, 1.1.1

options(download.file.method = "wininet"), setInternet2(TRUE), method = "curl" to enable https

nothing: the default is libcurl

FAQ 7.43: since R 4.2.0 the libcurl method is always available and the default for HTTPS

R 3.3.0, 4.2.0

download.file(url, destfile) on Windows for a binary file

download.file(url, destfile, mode = "wb")

text mode changes line endings on Windows

always

readLines(url("http://...")) for HTTPS sites, or getURL(url, ssl.verifypeer = FALSE)

readLines(url("https://...")), with certificates verified

verification is the default and should stay on

R 3.2.2

jsonlite::fromJSON(url) for an API that needs a header or a token

resp_body_json(req_perform(req), simplifyVector = TRUE)

fromJSON(url) can send no headers and shows no error body

httr2 1.0.0

unlist(lapply(urls, GET)) with a loop for many pages

req_perform_parallel(), req_perform_iterative()

paging helpers, max_active, error strategies

httr2 1.0.0

A test that calls the real service

local_mocked_responses()

no network in tests

httr2 1.0.0

Source: httr package documentation: Status

The httr package is at https://httr.r-lib.org/ and its status paragraph tells new users to use httr2; code that uses GET(), content() and stop_for_status() still runs, so read it as a description of the same ideas: a request is a URL plus configuration, a response has a status, headers and a body, and a status of 400 or more should become an error. RCurl is still on CRAN (RCurl on CRAN); its getURL() and postForm() are documented at RCurl package documentation: getURL. Neither package is run on this page.
